Many of the oddly high priced items sold on Amazon are priced incorrectly due to pricing services. Sellers on the Amazon platform can pay for services that will watch items similar to those being offered by the seller and will automatically adjust the prices according to the rules the seller sets up with the service. Some of these services are badly programmed and will sometimes get into pricing wars with other pricing services which artificially drive the price on some items up way beyond what anyone would pay. The two competing services adjust the item price according to their algorithmic rules and end up pushing the price to astronomical heights. This used to be more common, but many services fixed their systems or sellers stopped using them altogether due to bad pricing affecting sales. This does not account for all high priced items that are not worth much, but it does explain some of the most outrageous examples. There's a link below to a 2011 article about this happening to a book. As I said, it doesn't explain all occurrences of these high prices but it does offer a mundane explanation that doesn't require human trafficking or other money laundering to be included in the explanation.
